title: The Planes That Came Back: How Survivorship Bias Hijacks Your Judgment
description:
The military wanted to armor the bullet holes. One mathematician saw why that was exactly backwards — and named a thinking error that quietly shapes the decisions you make every day.

This is survivorship bias: drawing conclusions from the winners you can see, while the failures stay silent and uncounted. The founders who wrote books. The funds that advertise their returns. The friend who quit and made it. They are the planes that came back. Everything you're missing is in the silence.
